facts.statement: Pteraspis is an extinct genus of jawless fish belonging to the heterostracan group.
facts.quote: Pteraspis (from 'wing' or 'fin' and 'shield') is an extinct genus of pteraspidid heterostracan jawless fish.

facts.statement: Pteraspis lived during the Lochkovian to Eifelian epochs of the Devonian period in regions now known as the Americas and Europe.
facts.quote: It existed from the Lochkovian to Eifelian epochs of the Devonian period in areas that are now the Americas and Europe.

facts.statement: The genus Pteraspis was described by Kner in 1847.
facts.quote: authority: Kner, 1847

facts.statement: The type species for the genus Pteraspis is Cephalaspis rostrata.
facts.quote: type_species: Cephalaspis rostrata

facts.statement: Known species of Pteraspis include P. rostrata, P. dunensis, and P. crouchi.
facts.quote: subdivision: * P. rostrata (Agassiz, 1835) P. dunensis (Roemer, 1854) P. crouchi (Lankester, 1865)

facts.statement: Pteraspis is classified within the class Pteraspidomorphi.
facts.quote: classis: Pteraspidomorphi†

facts.statement: Pteraspis possessed protective armor plating on its front body and lacked fins except for a lobed tail.
facts.quote: Like other heterostracan fishes, Pteraspis had a protective armored plating covering the front of its body, and no fins other than a lobed tail.

facts.statement: Pteraspis featured two wing-like protrusions over its gills and a single protrusion on its back, derived from armored plates.
facts.quote: Despite this, Pteraspis had two wing-like protrusions derived from the armoured plates over its gills, and a single protrusion in the center of its back.

facts.statement: The wing-like protrusions and horn-like rostrum of Pteraspis suggest it had good swimming ability.
facts.quote: This, along with its horn-like rostrum, possibly indicates good swimming ability.

facts.statement: Pteraspis had stiff spines on its back, which may have served as protection against predators.
facts.quote: Pteraspis also has a series of stiff spines on its back, possibly as a form of protection against predators.

facts.statement: Pteraspis likely fed on shoals of plankton just beneath the ocean surface.
facts.quote: It is thought to have fed from shoals of plankton just under the ocean surface.

facts.statement: Fossil records of Pteraspis are found in both marine and freshwater environments.
facts.quote: Some records are found in association with marine fossils, while some others are found in freshwater environments.

facts.statement: The largest recorded specimens of Pteraspis reached an estimated length of 27 cm.
facts.quote: The largest recorded specimens of Pteraspis grew to an estimated length of 27 cm.

facts.statement: The authority for the genus Pteraspis is Kner, 1847.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Kner, 1847

facts.statement: Pteraspis belongs to the family Pteraspididae.
facts.quote: familia: Pteraspididae†

facts.statement: Pteraspis lived from 419.62 to 387.95 million years ago during the Lochkovian to Eifelian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Lochkovian to Eifelian (419.62 to 387.95 million years ago)

facts.statement: Like other heterostracan fish, Pteraspis had armored plating covering the front of its body.
facts.quote: Como otros peces heterostráceos, Pteraspis tenía un blindaje armado que cubría la parte frontal de su cuerpo.

facts.statement: Although it lacked fins beyond its lobed tail, Pteraspis is thought to have been a good swimmer due to rigid wing-like protrusions derived from its gill plates.
facts.quote: Aunque carecía de aletas más allá de su cola lobulada, se piensa que habría sido buen nadador, gracias a las protuberancias rígidas, como alas derivadas de sus láminas branquiales (partes de la armadura que cubrían sus agallas).

facts.statement: Its horn-shaped rostrum and wing-like protrusions made Pteraspis a highly aerodynamic form, perfect for swimming.
facts.quote: Esto, junto con el rostrum (proyección nasal) en forma de cuerno, hacía de Pteraspis una forma muy aerodinámica, una cualidad perfecta para un buen nadador.

facts.statement: It is believed that Pteraspis fed on shallow banks of plankton just below the ocean surface.
facts.quote: Se cree que se alimentaba de bancos de plancton poco profundos, apenas bajo la superficie del océano.
